sources: Yousef Jabareen (Joint List chairman) via AFP / Arab News; Times of Israel kingmakers analysis
fault_line: Should 19 Arab-party seats decide who governs Israel -- kingmaker legitimacy, or a government no Jewish bloc voted for?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen told AFP on Wednesday he is willing to support an alternative government from outside the coalition "with the aim of bringing down this government", but "we do not see the possibility of being part of an Israeli government coalition under the current political circumstances, particularly given the ongoing war in Gaza, the settlements in the West Bank" and other issues. [VERIFIED FACT] Standing count remains 85.6% / Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot bloc 48, Arab parties 19 (totw-20261028-2200-05); neither bloc reaches 61 without Arab support. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] ToI adds the mechanism: both Arab and Zionist opposition parties signal intent to use their parliamentary majority to replace Likud speaker Amir Ohana, giving the opposition control of the legislative agenda even under a caretaker Netanyahu, which could advance a state commission of inquiry into Oct 7, 2023; Ra'am would likely seek a ministerial/deputy post in the National Security Ministry before backing an anti-Netanyahu coalition. Reuters analysis (via Telegraph India, Oct 28) adds the caretaker mechanism: a caretaker PM retains war powers in law, with a duty of restraint and thinnest parliamentary oversight in the weeks after the new Knesset convenes.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct declared-tier families agree on the Wed outside-support offer and the 19-seat kingmaker maths.
sections.what_disputed: Jabareen made a materially similar outside-support pledge BEFORE the election (ToI Oct 11 report; JFeed pre-election video: support from outside, conditions incl. a budgeted anti-crime plan, an end to home demolitions, a diplomatic path to a Palestinian state) -- the Wed statement is a post-election REPEAT with 19 seats behind it, not a first-ever offer; do not present it as new terms. Mainstream opposition leaders have ruled out relying on Arab parties (Bennett, Feb; Liberman, Oct -- via JFeed/ToI background), and Eisenkot has said he will not form a government with them (2200 context) -- the 67-seat opposition+Arab arithmetic (48+19) is therefore available only if that refusal breaks. Likud's "stolen" fraud claim (2200-01) is Unverified and no evidence has been made public.
sections.why_matters: The count has not moved -- the power has: 19 seats now decide whether Netanyahu falls. Lead with Jabareen's own outside-support quote, then the 53-vs-61 maths, then the speaker-replacement mechanism. Proven-set adjacent (Israel election deadlock) with debate-bait fault line.
